title: Biggest Value Further Right
statement:
You get an integer array nums. Return a new array of the same length where position i holds the largest value found strictly to the right of index i in nums. The value at i itself does not count.

The last position has nothing to its right, so it holds -1.

examples.why: Right of 5 the largest is 9. Right of 9 itself only 1 and 4 remain, so the answer there is 4.
A single value has nothing to its right.
The second 6 is to the right of the first one, so it counts. The second 6 does not see itself, only the 1.

hints: The last answer is -1. Can the second-to-last answer be built from information you already have?
The answer at i is the maximum of nums[i + 1] and the answer at i + 1.
Walk from right to left with one running maximum. Write the running maximum first, then fold in the current value.

explain.intuition:
Scanning to the right of every index repeats the same work again and again: the part to the right of i is the part to the right of i + 1 plus one extra value, nums[i + 1]. So walk backwards and keep one number, the biggest value seen so far.

The order inside the loop is the whole trick. At index i, write the running maximum before adding nums[i] to it, because the answer must not include the value at i itself. Starting the running maximum at -1 gives the last position its answer for free.
steps: For i from n − 1 down to 0: set out[i] = best.
pitfalls: Updating best before writing out[i]. Then each position sees itself, and [4, 3] wrongly becomes [4, 3] instead of [3, -1].
Scanning forward and recomputing the maximum of the rest for each index. It is correct but O(n²).
Overwriting nums in place while reading it in a forward scan, so later answers read already replaced values.

solutions.title: Scan the rest for each index
solutions.idea: For every index, look at everything to its right and take the largest.

solutions.title: One backward pass with a running maximum
solutions.idea: Walk from the end, write the maximum seen so far, then fold in the current value.

followups: Return the index of the next larger value to the right instead of the largest one. Why does that need a stack?
Do it in place, overwriting nums, with O(1) extra space.
lcTitle: Replace Elements with Greatest Element on Right Side
